clusters.M1: Tensor-descriptor (TMA-style) operands lowered to scalar masked gathers
clusters.M2: Load cache policy under the write-flush protocol (streaming kernels)
clusters.M5: Narrow per-lane VMEM access and lost store vectorization
clusters.M7: Device-scope atomics serviced at the Infinity Fabric

description: Hand-written per-operator MI300X diagnosis from the 2026-10-05 analysis, copied verbatim. Field meanings are given in the docstring of the source diag.py (copied below).

1d_conv.alternative_explanation: Triton winner simply better tuned: tune gain 1.57/1.89 on MI300X, but the B200 relation was also autotuned
1d_conv.evidence: MIOpen igemm + 2 transposes (54%/36% of traced time FP16/FP32); PyTorch MI/B 1.91/3.16; Triton MI/B 0.67/0.71; Triton VALU util 85/70%, int32 67-68% of VALU
1d_conv.primary: PyTorch path: MIOpen layout transposes + igemm; Triton implicit GEMM wins
1d_conv.secondary: Triton kernel VALU-bound on index reconstruction (M4)

2d_conv.alternative_explanation: Triton tile not optimal; no evidence Triton can reach Winograd arithmetic count with implicit GEMM
2d_conv.evidence: PyTorch = single MIOpen Winograd F(2,3) asm kernel; FP32 Winograd slower than B200 (MI/B 2.63)

2d_max_pooling.alternative_explanation: Cache policy (M2) could also contribute; not ablated
2d_max_pooling.evidence: 18 ushort loads/lane, coalescing 30%, 72-75% PC samples on VMEM loads (ARBITER_NOT_WIN 58-63%); Triton MI/B 1.5-1.7 vs PyTorch 0.93-1.09
2d_max_pooling.primary: Window gather issued as 2-byte per-lane loads; VMEM arbitration stalls

3d_conv.alternative_explanation: CK kernel choice may be shape-specific; only the profiled shape traced
3d_conv.evidence: CK grouped conv XDL + 4 transposes (32%/8%); PyTorch MI/B 2.76/7.88; Triton MI/B 0.49/0.53
3d_conv.primary: PyTorch path: CK conv + transposes; FP32 CK path 7.9x slower than B200 cuDNN

argmax.alternative_explanation: Row-loop structure / grid shape rather than policy; nt verified only for the mean instantiation of reduce_kernel
argmax.evidence: ATen reduce_kernel; VMEM latency 7,100-16,000 cycles; reversal FP32 1.79 -> 0.79
argmax.primary: Memory-latency-bound row reduction; PyTorch reduce path uses nt loads
argmax.secondary: VMEM latency 7,100-16,000 cycles; 66-68% of PC samples on s_waitcnt

batch_normalization.alternative_explanation: Triton-side slowness (MI/B 3.0-3.1 FP16/BF16) partly offsets; PyTorch kernel not counter-profiled
batch_normalization.evidence: ATen BN statistics kernel 90% of reference; PyTorch MI/B 2.7-4.0; Triton block-sum grid 313 WGs, VGPR 164-234
batch_normalization.primary: PyTorch BN statistics kernel slow on ROCm (2.7-4.0x B200)

batched_matmul.alternative_explanation: Small per-batch GEMMs (640^2) also limit hipBLASLt comparison; no batched pointer experiment
batched_matmul.evidence: ushort/dword scalar loads, coalescing 25%, MFMA 3.5-4.0%, PC 48-78% on VMEM loads; same signature as the experiment-verified matmul
batched_matmul.primary: Descriptor loads -> scalar 2/4-byte gathers; MFMA util 3.5-4.0%

bitonic_sort.alternative_explanation: Higher per-launch overhead on ROCm for 300 launches (kernel time only, so excluded by Proton)
bitonic_sort.evidence: PyTorch: 15,903 eager kernels; Triton step loads ushort/dword, 43% ARBITER_NOT_WIN; Triton MI/B 1.7-2.3 vs PyTorch 1.08-1.10
bitonic_sort.primary: Eager reference dominates (huge Triton win on both GPUs)
bitonic_sort.secondary: Partner loads narrow & masked -> VMEM issue-bound (M5)

block_sparse_attention.alternative_explanation: Inductor's flex kernel exploits block mask differently (algorithmic difference within Triton)
block_sparse_attention.evidence: ushort loads x160, 512 regs, 20 B scratch, occupancy 1, MFMA 2.5%; Inductor Triton 0.24 ms vs 0.56 ms
block_sparse_attention.primary: Descriptor loads + 512-register kernel with scratch spill; Inductor Triton 2.35x faster

cross_entropy.alternative_explanation: FP16 gap could reflect PyTorch FP16 path improvement (MI/B 1.23)
cross_entropy.evidence: PyTorch 3 kernels (softmax_warp_forward, nll_loss, fill); Triton 1 kernel/row, DPP reductions; FP16 1 element/lane
cross_entropy.primary: Fusion of 3 eager kernels into one row-wise kernel preserved
cross_entropy.secondary: FP16: 1 element/lane (2-byte loads) at wave64 granularity

dequantize_rowwise.evidence: PyTorch 3 elementwise kernels; Triton dwordx2/x4, 65% HBM; ratio 6.41 vs 5.95
dequantize_rowwise.primary: Fusion of eager chain; Triton at 65% HBM

destindex.alternative_explanation: Load policy (M2) also affects the load side; not ablated
destindex.evidence: LLIR: 4 x buffer.store.i8 per lane (INT8), short stores (FP16); B200: 128-bit stores (paper); Triton HBM 48-75% vs 55-97%
destindex.primary: Scatter store not vectorized on gfx942 (per-element byte/short stores)

dropout.evidence: PyTorch 2 vectorized kernels; Triton single kernel at 60-63% HBM; B200 1.5-1.6 -> 1.09-1.14
dropout.primary: Fusion advantage eroded by streaming load-policy gap

flash_attention.alternative_explanation: AOTriton uses a different tiling/pipelining (not only load lowering); spill share not isolated
flash_attention.evidence: ushort loads x128, 512 regs, 268 B scratch, occupancy 1, MFMA 7.5%; AOTriton attn_fwd 45.5 ms vs 142.9 ms
flash_attention.primary: Descriptor loads + 512 registers, 268 B scratch spill, occupancy 1
flash_attention.secondary: AOTriton (also Triton) 3.1x faster: abstraction not the limit

flash_decode.alternative_explanation: PyTorch eager kernels parallelize over sequence; Triton design choice (split) rather than DSL
flash_decode.evidence: grid 16 WGs x 2 waves, ~30 resident waves; T/P 6.34 -> 0.59 with seq_len; PyTorch 20 kernels
flash_decode.primary: 16-workgroup grid: serial latency-bound loop; Triton loses at long seq

fused_activation.primary: Fusion advantage eroded by streaming load-policy gap

gaussian_blur.alternative_explanation: cuDNN choice on B200 may be suboptimal for this filter; not examined
gaussian_blur.evidence: MIOpen igemm 99% of reference; PyTorch MI/B 0.29/0.40; Triton VALU util 77-87%, 50 2/4-byte loads/lane
gaussian_blur.primary: PyTorch path faster than on B200 (MIOpen 2.5-3.4x faster than B200 path)

histogramming.alternative_explanation: Contention on few bins / partial layout; no LDS-privatized control experiment
histogramming.evidence: 67.1 M vL1D atomics -> 4.19 M L2 = 4.19 M fabric atomic requests (100% atomic traffic), latency ~367 cyc, 64% PC on atomics; T/P 2.27 -> 0.27
histogramming.primary: All L2 atomics forwarded to Infinity Fabric; 64% of PC samples on atomics

interleave.evidence: ATen manual_unroll scalar dword without nt (ATT, FP32); Triton dwordx4; 1.8-2.2x
interleave.primary: Triton vectorized copy beats non-vectorized ATen copy
interleave.pt: ATen elementwise_kernel_manual_unroll x2 (scalar dword, no nt)

jacobi_stencil_2d.evidence: PyTorch 6 kernels; Triton ushort/dword neighbour loads, 34-56% HBM
jacobi_stencil_2d.primary: Fusion of eager stencil preserved; 2/4-byte neighbour loads

kl_divergence.evidence: PyTorch 4 kernels; Triton 67% HBM; ratio 2.65 vs 2.84
kl_divergence.primary: Fusion preserved, similar ratio on both GPUs

l2_norm.primary: Fusion preserved but halved; Triton at 57-60% HBM

b200_table5.primary_diagnosis: Fixed issue cost + wider write back

layernorm.evidence: ATen vectorized_layer_norm without nt (ATT FP16); Triton 73-82% HBM
layernorm.primary: Both near the memory floor (Triton 73-82% HBM)

leaky_relu.evidence: ATen vectorized kernel (nt inferred); Triton 63-75% HBM; 1.0 -> 0.73-0.83

linear_self_attention.alternative_explanation: PyTorch uses 15 kernels incl. hipBLASLt; GEMM stages affected by M1
linear_self_attention.evidence: z_kernel 8 WGs (36%), kv_gemm 64 WGs (49%), descriptor dword loads; B200: 8-CTA column reduction ~57%
linear_self_attention.primary: z_kernel (8 WGs, 36%) and kv_gemm (64 WGs, 49%) under-fill 304 CUs

matmul_fp32_fp16_fp8.alternative_explanation: Search space without AMD knobs; ruled out by same-config experiment
matmul_fp32_fp16_fp8.evidence: TTIR pointer rewrite with runtime i64 strides; TTGIR threadsPerWarp=[64,1]; ushort loads; MFMA 3.7-4.5%; experiment 6.7x/3.35x
matmul_fp32_fp16_fp8.primary: Descriptor loads -> scalar gathers; pointer variant 3.4-6.7x faster

matmul_int8.evidence: Reference = FP32 Cijk GEMM (62%) + unpack; PyTorch MI/B 0.59; Triton ubyte loads, MFMA 2.7%
matmul_int8.primary: FP32 reference runs on FP32 MFMA (1.7x faster than B200 ref); Triton int8 descriptor path

matrix_copy.evidence: ATen vectorized kernel (nt inferred); Triton 64-68% HBM (16/32-bit); INT8 parity
matrix_copy.pt: ATen vectorized_elementwise_kernel (nt loads; int8 path without nt)

matrix_transpose.evidence: ATen manual_unroll scalar dword, no nt (ATT FP32); Triton LDS 16-64 KB + dwordx4
matrix_transpose.primary: LDS-staged vectorized transpose beats scalar ATen copy
matrix_transpose.pt: ATen manual_unroll copy (scalar dword, no nt)

mean_reduction.alternative_explanation: Row-loop memory-level parallelism; not ablated with .cg
mean_reduction.evidence: ATen reduce_kernel with nt loads (ATT FP32); Triton VMEM latency 10,200-16,600 cycles; 89% PC on VMEM loads
mean_reduction.primary: Memory-latency-bound row reduction vs nt-load ATen reduce
mean_reduction.secondary: 89% of PC samples on vector-memory loads (bf16, fp32)

moe_topk_gating.evidence: Triton single-wave rows, DPP 38-44 + 8 ds_bpermute; PyTorch gatherTopK + sort + softmax
moe_topk_gating.pt: ATen gatherTopK + bitonic KV sort + softmax

mul2.evidence: ATen vectorized kernel (nt inferred); Triton 64-65% HBM; INT8 parity
mul2.pt: ATen vectorized_elementwise_kernel (nt loads; int8 without nt)

quantize_global.evidence: ATen vectorized float16 copy (nt inferred); 59% HBM

radix_sort.evidence: rocPRIM radix sort 90% of reference; Triton 66% HBM; ratios 0.62 vs 0.69
radix_sort.primary: Vendor sort algorithm wins on both GPUs by a similar margin

relu.evidence: ATen vectorized kernel with nt (ATT FP16); INT8 kernel without nt; FP16 1.12 -> 0.85
relu.primary: Streaming load-policy gap (0.78-0.87x); INT8 Triton wins

reverse_array.evidence: ATen flip scalar dword, no nt (ATT FP32); Triton ushort/ubyte for 16/8-bit
reverse_array.primary: Triton wins vs non-vectorized flip; 16/8-bit reversal uses narrow loads
reverse_array.pt: ATen flip (index_elementwise, scalar dword, no nt)

rmsnorm.evidence: ATen vectorized_layer_norm (RMS) without nt (inferred); Triton 73-84% HBM
rmsnorm.primary: Near parity on both; Triton 73-84% HBM

rope.primary: Fusion preserved (3.6-4.3x) but smaller than B200 (8-13x)

sigmoid.alternative_explanation: PyTorch FP16 sigmoid compute-bound; not profiled
sigmoid.evidence: FP32 0.71 vs FP16/BF16 ~1.0; ATen FP16 sigmoid itself below the memory floor (inferred)
sigmoid.primary: FP32 load-policy gap (0.71x); FP16/BF16 near parity
sigmoid.secondary: Dtype trend opposite to B200's cuTile trend

softmax.alternative_explanation: Online-softmax two-pass structure vs PyTorch; PyTorch kernel not counter-profiled
softmax.evidence: ATen cunn_SoftMaxForwardGmem (no nt) PyTorch MI/B 0.68 FP16; Triton VALU util 47%, 42% HBM
softmax.primary: ATen softmax relatively stronger on MI300X; Triton kernel partly VALU-bound

streamk_matmul.alternative_explanation: B200 first_wave loop diagnosis; first_wave is only 8% here
streamk_matmul.evidence: full_tiles 92% of profile, ushort/dword scalar loads, MFMA 2.9-7.9%; first_wave 6.4 M fabric atomics; FP32 164 B spill
streamk_matmul.primary: Descriptor loads -> scalar gathers in full_tiles (92% of time)

swiglu.primary: Fusion preserved but eroded by load-policy gap

top_k_selection.evidence: tl.topk: DPP 412 + 80 ds_bpermute, LDS conflicts 4.5/access; PyTorch rocPRIM merge sort (21 kernels)
top_k_selection.primary: tl.topk lowers to DPP/ds_bpermute network; similar sweep ratio

vector_add.alternative_explanation: Load width / per-lane work: ruled out by config sweep
vector_add.evidence: ATT: ATen dwordx4 nt loads; Triton default 0.62x in all configs; .cg loads 1.0-1.08x; read-only flush 0.90x
vector_add.primary: Streaming load-policy gap (0.63-0.66x); recovered by .cg loads
vector_add.secondary: best default-policy config 0.625x of 26 tried (20 grid configs + persistent)

weight_dequant.evidence: constexpr N -> multiply-high index math (3 v_int_mul); Triton 74-85% HBM; PyTorch 8 kernels
weight_dequant.primary: Fusion preserved; constexpr index math stays cheap (74-85% HBM)

source_docstring:
Hand-written per-operator diagnosis for MI300X (evidence in data/*.json, exp/*.json, att/*).
Fields:
  b200: (primary diagnosis, PyTorch path, Q_o) copied from the B200 paper Table 5 (tab:app-rq3-map).
  pt:   PyTorch path on MI300X (from the rocprofv3 kernel trace of one reference call).
  mech: MI300X mechanism cluster id (see CLUSTERS).
  primary / secondary: short text for the diagnosis map.
  nature: one or more of the requested categories.
  rel:  B200 -> MI300X relationship class.
  conf: High / Medium / Low.   pri: High / Medium / Low / Control.
